newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended slightly lower on Friday after a see-saw session in low volume ahead of Monday's French audit, dealers said.
"Today, there's no story. It started down, it was up and then, it was pulled down by foreign markets," a dealer in Madrid said. "But also late trade losses were without much importance".
Another dealer said the market was likely to focus on France on Monday, when the result of the public budget audit is due.
"If the French public accounts audit shows a massive hole in finances, look for Europe's high yield sector, including Spain, to suffer," a Bear Stearns note to clients said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended near 64 basis points versus 63 basis points this morning.
Other than fears of overspill from foreign markets, dealers said there was little fresh domestic news expected for the bond market.
May's industrial production, which grew a non-calendar adjusted 3.1 percent in the year, was weaker both than April's 17.7 percent and the market consensus for 6.4 percent.
But it was considered another confirmation that a recent pick-up in the Spanish economy showed no signs of overheating.
